title: Google Cloud SQL
description: Monitor Google Cloud SQL with metrics and logs
overview:
### Monitor Google Cloud SQL with FuseScope

Collect Cloud SQL metrics from Cloud Monitoring with the OpenTelemetry `googlecloudmonitoring` receiver and view CPU, memory, disk, network, connections and replica lag on an out of the box dashboard.

Collect Cloud SQL logs by routing them from Cloud Logging to a Pub/Sub topic and reading the subscription with the `googlecloudpubsub` receiver. Installed log pipelines parse the MySQL error log and the PostgreSQL log.

Covers Cloud SQL for MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server. To collect engine metrics as well, add the MySQL or PostgreSQL integration pointed at the instance.

configuration.title: Prerequisites
configuration.instructions:
## Before You Begin

To collect Cloud SQL metrics and logs, you need the following.

### Prepare Google Cloud

The commands below use the [gcloud CLI](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install) and read the project from `GCP_PROJECT_ID`:

```bash
export GCP_PROJECT_ID="<project-id>"
```

- **Enable the APIs** in the project that holds the Cloud SQL instances:
  ```sh
  gcloud services enable monitoring.googleapis.com logging.googleapis.com pubsub.googleapis.com \
    --project "$GCP_PROJECT_ID"
  ```

- **Create a service account for the collector**
  ```sh
  gcloud iam service-accounts create fusescope-collector \
    --project "$GCP_PROJECT_ID" \
    --display-name "FuseScope collector"
  ```

- **Grant it the roles it needs**

  | Role | On | Used for |
  |---|---|---|
  | `roles/monitoring.viewer` | project | reading metrics from Cloud Monitoring |
  | `roles/pubsub.subscriber` | the log subscription | pulling logs from Pub/Sub, granted in the **Collect Logs** step |

  ```sh
  gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding "$GCP_PROJECT_ID" \
    --member "serviceAccount:fusescope-collector@$GCP_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
    --role roles/monitoring.viewer
  ```

  The person running the setup needs `roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin`, `roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin`, `roles/pubsub.admin` and `roles/logging.configWriter`, or `roles/owner`.

- **Give the collector the service account's credentials**
  The receivers use [Application Default Credentials](https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials).
  - On Compute Engine, attach the service account to the VM.
  - On GKE, bind it to the collector's Kubernetes service account with [Workload Identity Federation](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/workload-identity).
  - Elsewhere, create a key and point `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` at it. Store the key file as a secret and keep it out of version control.
    ```sh
    gcloud iam service-accounts keys create fusescope-collector-key.json \
      --iam-account "fusescope-collector@$GCP_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
    ```
    ```bash
    export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/etc/otelcol-contrib/fusescope-collector-key.json
    ```

### Prepare the OpenTelemetry Collector

- **Run an OpenTelemetry Collector**
  If needed, [install the OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib distribution](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/installation/). The configs below are validated with `otelcol-contrib` v0.163; older releases may lack the `google_cloud_logentry_encoding` extension.

  Make sure you can pass config files, environment variables and command line flags to it.

- **Allow outbound HTTPS** from the collector to `monitoring.googleapis.com` and `pubsub.googleapis.com`.

configuration.title: Collect Metrics
configuration.instructions:
### Collect Cloud SQL Metrics

The `googlecloudmonitoring` receiver lists time series from the Cloud Monitoring API. Each metric keeps its Cloud Monitoring name, such as `cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/cpu/utilization`, and the `cloudsql_database` resource labels (`project_id`, `database_id`, `region`) become resource attributes.

Cloud Monitoring bills API reads; the default interval below keeps the cost low. The minimum is 60s.

#### Create collector config file

Save the following config in a file named `gcp-cloudsql-metrics-collection-config.yaml`.

```yaml
receivers:
  googlecloudmonitoring:
    project_id: ${env:GCP_PROJECT_ID}
    collection_interval: 120s
    metrics_list:
      - metric_name: "cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/cpu/utilization"
      - metric_name: "cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/memory/utilization"
      - metric_name: "cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/disk/utilization"
      - metric_name: "cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/disk/bytes_used"
      - metric_name: "cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/disk/read_ops_count"
      - metric_name: "cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/disk/write_ops_count"
      - metric_name: "cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/network/received_bytes_count"
      - metric_name: "cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/network/sent_bytes_count"
      - metric_name: "cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/network/connections"
      - metric_name: "cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/postgresql/num_backends"
      - metric_name: "cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/postgresql/transaction_count"
      - metric_name: "cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/mysql/queries"
      - metric_name: "cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/replication/replica_lag"
      - metric_name: "cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/up"

processors:
  batch:
    send_batch_size: 10000
    timeout: 10s

exporters:
  otlp/fusescope:
    endpoint: ${env:OTLP_DESTINATION_ENDPOINT}
    tls:
      # set to false when the FuseScope endpoint uses TLS
      insecure: true

service:
  pipelines:
    metrics/gcp_cloudsql:
      receivers: [googlecloudmonitoring]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp/fusescope]
```

To collect from several projects, add one `googlecloudmonitoring/<name>` receiver per project, and grant the service account `roles/monitoring.viewer` in each.

#### Set Environment Variables

Set the following environment variables in your collector environment:

```bash

# project that holds the Cloud SQL instances
export GCP_PROJECT_ID="<project-id>"

# OTLP gRPC endpoint of your FuseScope collector, see https://fuseone-io.github.io/fusescope-docs/sending-data/otlp/
export OTLP_DESTINATION_ENDPOINT="<fusescope-otel-collector-host>:4317"

```

#### Use collector config file

Pass the config file to your collector with the following flag:
```bash
--config gcp-cloudsql-metrics-collection-config.yaml
```
Note: the collector can use multiple config files, specified by multiple occurrences of the --config flag.

configuration.title: Collect Logs
configuration.instructions:
### Collect Cloud SQL Logs

Cloud SQL writes its logs to Cloud Logging. A log sink routes them to a Pub/Sub topic, and the `googlecloudpubsub` receiver pulls them from a subscription. The `google_cloud_logentry_encoding` extension turns each `LogEntry` into an OpenTelemetry log: timestamp, severity, trace context, labels and the payload as the body.

#### Route the logs to Pub/Sub

```sh
# topic and pull subscription for the logs
gcloud pubsub topics create fusescope-cloudsql-logs --project "$GCP_PROJECT_ID"
gcloud pubsub subscriptions create fusescope-cloudsql-logs \
  --project "$GCP_PROJECT_ID" \
  --topic fusescope-cloudsql-logs \
  --ack-deadline 60 \
  --message-retention-duration 1d

# sink that sends Cloud SQL logs to the topic
gcloud logging sinks create fusescope-cloudsql-logs \
  "pubsub.googleapis.com/projects/$GCP_PROJECT_ID/topics/fusescope-cloudsql-logs" \
  --project "$GCP_PROJECT_ID" \
  --log-filter 'resource.type="cloudsql_database"'

# let the sink publish to the topic
gcloud pubsub topics add-iam-policy-binding fusescope-cloudsql-logs \
  --project "$GCP_PROJECT_ID" \
  --member "$(gcloud logging sinks describe fusescope-cloudsql-logs --project "$GCP_PROJECT_ID" --format 'value(writerIdentity)')" \
  --role roles/pubsub.publisher

# let the collector pull from the subscription
gcloud pubsub subscriptions add-iam-policy-binding fusescope-cloudsql-logs \
  --project "$GCP_PROJECT_ID" \
  --member "serviceAccount:fusescope-collector@$GCP_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role roles/pubsub.subscriber
```

Narrow `--log-filter` to keep costs down, for example `resource.type="cloudsql_database" AND severity>=WARNING`. For the slow query log of Cloud SQL for MySQL, set the `slow_query_log` and `log_output=FILE` database flags.

#### Create collector config file

Save the following config in a file named `gcp-cloudsql-logs-collection-config.yaml`.

```yaml
extensions:
  google_cloud_logentry_encoding:
    handle_json_payload_as: json

receivers:
  googlecloudpubsub:
    project: ${env:GCP_PROJECT_ID}
    subscription: ${env:GCP_PUBSUB_SUBSCRIPTION}
    encoding: google_cloud_logentry_encoding

processors:
  attributes/gcp_cloudsql:
    actions:
      - key: source
        value: gcp_cloudsql
        action: insert
  batch:
    send_batch_size: 10000
    send_batch_max_size: 11000
    timeout: 10s

exporters:
  otlp/fusescope:
    endpoint: ${env:OTLP_DESTINATION_ENDPOINT}
    tls:
      # set to false when the FuseScope endpoint uses TLS
      insecure: true

service:
  extensions: [google_cloud_logentry_encoding]
  pipelines:
    logs/gcp_cloudsql:
      receivers: [googlecloudpubsub]
      processors: [attributes/gcp_cloudsql, batch]
      exporters: [otlp/fusescope]
```

#### Set Environment Variables

Set the following environment variables in your collector environment:

```bash

# project that holds the Pub/Sub subscription
export GCP_PROJECT_ID="<project-id>"

# full name of the subscription created above
export GCP_PUBSUB_SUBSCRIPTION="projects/<project-id>/subscriptions/fusescope-cloudsql-logs"

# OTLP gRPC endpoint of your FuseScope collector, see https://fuseone-io.github.io/fusescope-docs/sending-data/otlp/
export OTLP_DESTINATION_ENDPOINT="<fusescope-otel-collector-host>:4317"

```

#### Use collector config file

Pass the config file to your collector with the following flag:
```bash
--config gcp-cloudsql-logs-collection-config.yaml
```
Note: the collector can use multiple config files, specified by multiple occurrences of the --config flag.

#### Parsed attributes

The log name (for example `cloudsql.googleapis.com%2Fmysql.err`) is in the `cloud.resource_id` resource attribute, the instance in `gcp.label.database_id`.

| Log | Attributes |
|---|---|
| MySQL error log (`mysql.err`) | `thread_id`, `error_code`, `subsystem` |
| PostgreSQL log (`postgres.log`) | `pid`, `db_name`, `db_user` |

metrics.name: cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/cpu/utilization
metrics.description: Fraction of the reserved CPU in use.

metrics.name: cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/memory/utilization
metrics.description: Fraction of the instance memory in use.

metrics.name: cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/disk/utilization
metrics.description: Fraction of the data disk quota in use.

metrics.name: cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/disk/read_ops_count
metrics.description: Delta count of data disk read IO operations.

metrics.name: cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/disk/write_ops_count
metrics.description: Delta count of data disk write IO operations.

metrics.name: cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/network/received_bytes_count
metrics.description: Delta count of bytes received through the network.

metrics.name: cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/network/sent_bytes_count
metrics.description: Delta count of bytes sent through the network.

metrics.name: cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/network/connections
metrics.description: Connections to the instance. MySQL and SQL Server only.

metrics.name: cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/postgresql/transaction_count
metrics.description: Delta count of committed and rolled back transactions. PostgreSQL only.

metrics.name: cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/mysql/queries
metrics.description: Delta count of statements executed by the server. MySQL only.

metrics.name: cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/replication/replica_lag
metrics.description: Seconds a read replica is behind its primary.

metrics.name: cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/up
metrics.description: 1 when the instance is up, 0 otherwise.

pipelines.name: Cloud SQL MySQL error log
pipelines.description: Parses the MySQL error log of Cloud SQL instances: thread id, error code and subsystem.

pipelines.name: Cloud SQL PostgreSQL log
pipelines.description: Parses the PostgreSQL log of Cloud SQL instances: process id, database and user.

display.name: Cloud SQL overview
display.description: CPU, memory, disk, network, connections and replication of Google Cloud SQL instances.

spec.queryValue:
SELECT JSONExtractString(labels, 'database_id') AS `database_id`
FROM signoz_metrics.distributed_time_series_v4_1day
WHERE metric_name = 'cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/up'
GROUP BY `database_id`

display.name: Memory utilization
display.description: Memory in use, as a fraction of the instance memory.

display.name: Transactions (PostgreSQL)
display.description: Committed and rolled back transactions per second.

display.name: Replica lag
display.description: Seconds a read replica is behind its primary.

display.name: Disk write operations
display.description: Data disk write IO operations per second.

display.name: Disk utilization
display.description: Data disk in use, as a fraction of the disk quota.

display.name: Disk read operations
display.description: Data disk read IO operations per second.
